economic-objectives-and-the-role-of-gove.d: Economic Objectives and the Role of Government
terms: Fiscal policy
Use of government spending and taxation to influence aggregate demand; Treasury's Budget tool.
Macroeconomic objectives
UK government targets: low and stable inflation, full employment, economic growth, balance of payments equilibrium.
Monetary policy
Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee changes interest rates and uses quantitative easing to control inflation.
Privatisation
Transferring state-owned enterprises to private ownership; major UK programme in 1980s under Thatcher.
Public sector
Government-owned activities like NHS, state schools and roads; funded by taxation and borrowing.
Regulation
Rules set by government or regulators (Ofgem, Ofcom) to correct market failure and protect consumers.

international-trade-and-the-global-econo.d: International Trade and the Global Economy
terms: Comparative advantage
Ricardo (1817): countries gain from trade by specialising in goods of lowest opportunity cost.
Free trade
Trade without tariffs, quotas or other barriers; promoted by WTO rules.
Globalisation
Growing economic interdependence via trade, investment and technology; UK trade-to-GDP ratio around 64% (2023).
Imports and exports
Imports are goods/services purchased from abroad; exports are sold abroad; difference is trade balance.
Protectionism
Restricting imports via tariffs (taxes), quotas (limits) or subsidies to domestic producers.
Tariff
Tax on imported goods, raising their price and reducing demand for them.
Economics
Study of how scarce resources are allocated among competing uses to satisfy unlimited human wants.
Factors of production
Four resources: land, labour, capital and enterprise; combined to produce goods and services.
Macroeconomics
Study of the economy as a whole: GDP, inflation, unemployment, balance of payments.
Microeconomics
Study of individual markets and decisions of households and firms; e.g. price of a single product.
Scarcity
Fundamental problem that resources are limited while wants are unlimited, forcing choices.
Smith (1776)
Adam Smith's 'Wealth of Nations' argued the invisible hand of market exchange allocates resources efficiently.

the-role-of-markets-and-money.d: The Role of Markets and Money
terms: Competitive market
Many buyers and sellers, homogeneous goods, free entry; prices reflect supply and demand.
Consumer surplus
Difference between what consumers are willing to pay and what they actually pay; area below demand, above price.
Market
Any arrangement where buyers and sellers interact to exchange goods, services or factors at a price.
Market failure
When market does not allocate resources efficiently; sources include externalities, public goods, information failures.
Monopoly
Single firm dominates a market; price maker; can restrict output to raise prices.
Price mechanism
Smith's invisible hand: prices signal scarcity, incentivise production and ration goods.
